text:
kevin: Heads-up: ACME reported batch /v1/rerank returning scores that don't align with per-query candidate lists. They say candidate IDs appear shifted. High severity, customer-facing.
sophie: Can you paste the payload + response? Is this only for multi-query batches or single-query too?
kevin: Pasting a minimal repro they sent (sanitized):\n```json\n{\n  "queries": [\n    {"id": "q1", "text": "How to reset password"},\n    {"id": "q2", "text": "Password policy"}\n  ],\n  "candidates": [\n    [ {"id":"c1","text":"Reset steps"}, {"id":"c2","text":"Reset via email"} ],\n    [ {"id":"c3","text":"Policy doc"} ]\n  ]\n}\n```\nExpected: scores map to c1,c2 for q1 and c3 for q2.
Actual response (truncated):
```json
{"scores": [0.87, 0.45, 0.99], "candidate_ids": ["c1","c2","c3"], "mapping":"flattened"}
```
Customer sees score 0.99 applied to their q1 second candidate instead of q2's only candidate.
maria: Are they sending application/json or JSONL? Any middle proxy that might concat/stream? Also any limits (max candidates) hit?
alex: I searched logs for their request id and saw our inbound parser recorded `candidates_count:3` but `per_query_counts` header missing. Looks like our runtime fell back to flattening when streaming flag was set. eng-ml-bot: auto-detect -> request_schema_mismatch for rnk-20260315-7a3f: missing per_query_counts; fallback path engaged.
jordan: We've seen this pattern when client libraries chunk candidate lists for large inputs (axios multipart or aggregator that inserts newlines). If the client splits arrays and the gateway re-assembles incorrectly, indices can shift. Repro in our infra: when candidate arrays > 512 we convert to multipart, and older proxies omitted boundary markers.
kevin: Customer says it happens even with small payloads (3 candidates). I pulled raw bytes from their proxy log: there were stray `\n` characters between array elements which our streaming parser treated as separate JSON entities.
sophie: Could be a JSONL->JSON conversion bug upstream. Our parser accepts either JSON or JSONL but the streaming path expects `per_query_counts` header when JSONL is used.
alex: Stacktrace points to batch_rerank_serializer in eng-runtime: when `is_streaming` === true we serialize candidate indices flat and rely on per_query_counts header. If header missing, fallback computes offsets by splitting based on token separators — fragile.
maria: They also reported intermittent 500s and spikes in latency during repro. If fallback is slower it may cause retries from their side, reshuffling batches and causing more misalignment and extra billing.
kevin: Repro steps I ran locally produce the issue too. Curl I used:\n```bash\ncurl -s -X POST \ \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' \ \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ \n  -d '{"queries":[{"id":"q1","text":"foo"},{"id":"q2","text":"bar"}],"candidates":[[{"id":"c1"},{"id":"c2"}], [{"id":"c3"}] ]}' \ \n  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank/batch\n```\nExpected mapping: q1->[c1,c2], q2->[c3]. Got flat mapping instead.
eng-runtime: Assigned. Please attach full request_id and the raw request body. We'll reproduce in staging with the exact byte stream and our streaming flags.
kevin: Request id: rnk-20260315-7a3f. Raw body attached to the case. Also FYI: customer flagged billing spike due to retries — they want a partial credit until fix.
eng-runtime: Investigating now. Early findings: if `per_query_counts` header is absent and `is_streaming` true, serializer currently attempts best-effort offset calc. We'll add a defensive check: if sum(candidate_lengths) != scores_length, return 400 instead of best-effort mapping. Also preparing a hotfix to compute per-query offsets from nested arrays when possible.
sophie: :thumbsup: Please post PR and ETA. Customer expects patch today.
eng-runtime: PR #4821 opened (https://git.internal/redwood/eng-runtime/pull/4821). Deploying to staging in ~2h, prod after verification. ETA ~6 hours for prod.
kevin: Forwarding workaround to customer: flatten candidates client-side and include explicit `per_query_counts` array, e.g. `per_query_counts: [2,1]`. That avoids ambiguous parsing. cc @maria for billing follow-up.
maria: I'll open billing ticket and propose a pro-rated credit. Support case #SC-45521 created.
kevin: Thanks everyone. I'll update the customer when prod deploy is complete and close out the support thread.
